purpose: Learn the held mug body midpoint from fixed-view RGB silhouette geometry before adding visual motor correction.

data.source_episodes: All 41 existing original mug demonstration episodes; no exposed 920x/960x physical trace supplies training examples.
data.method: Offline posed renders only: interpolate existing teacher motor endpoints, perturb right joints, place the mug near the calibrated tool contact with independent pose variation, and render without stepping physics. Absent cases move the mug outside every camera. These are synthetic perception examples, not physically valid grasps or evidence of manipulation. Preserve exact qpos, episode, exposure, labels, image hashes and encoded features for every state.

observer.classical_front_end: Unchanged teal RGB component rule and fixed projected workspace ROI from the visibility protocol. Each view encodes availability, area, centroid, bounding box and a 16x16 area-resized component mask (264 floats). Require at least two views with at least 60 pixels.
observer.inference_inputs: RGB images and fixed camera calibration only. No robot state, object pose, segmentation, depth, teacher, inverse solver or action retrieval.

fit.loss: Mean squared normalized XYZ midpoint error on present, RGB-accepted training states only; no development/evaluation gradients.
fit.selection: After both declared checkpoints, among those passing the development gate select lowest p95 3D error, then lower maximum error, then earlier update. No extra fit or threshold revision.

evaluation: Generate fresh synthetic evaluation only after a frozen checkpoint passes development and FP32 OpenVINO CPU parity. Test all 512 states once. After that, also score all 144 saved states of the visibility diagnostic as exposed physical-state regression, without fitting or gate relaxation. A passing synthetic gate alone does not demonstrate continuous control or physical generalization. No physical controller is selected by this protocol.

export.device: OpenVINO CPU FP32; measured PC identity required, never claim Intel execution from AMD/NVIDIA

stop_rule: Finish the one declared fit and both development scores. If neither checkpoint passes, preserve both and stop before export/fresh perception. If fresh perception fails, preserve every outcome and stop before any motor-control integration. Any follow-up needs a new protocol and new data selection.
retention: Preserve all generated examples, failed/refused observations, both checkpoints, all metrics, exact compact render recipes and labels, image hashes, source hashes and actual exported IR where permitted. No overwrite or deletion. GitHub and HF stay private; the user alone presses final Submit.
